_about: Where the models are served. Two machines, run by two people, with two engines.

An environment is one serving snapshot: an engine at one version, on one class of GPU, at one number format. Change any of those and it is a different environment, with its own key, because published work finds swings of tens of points across configurations of the same weights.

Every model names the environment it is served in, under `deployments` in models.json, and its serve file must agree with that environment about the number format and the engine's flags. `ipb.runner.serving check` refuses a disagreement.

engine_profile names the rules in ipb.runner.serving that were read out of that engine's source: which flags it has, and what it does to a conversation it cannot carry. Two environments on the same engine version share a profile.
reasoning_separation says who splits a model's thinking from its answer. `server` is vLLM's reasoning parser; `client` is ipb.runner.response, for an engine with no parser that can do it safely.
Facts checked on 2026-09-12 against the source of each engine version. Reasons for every line: README.md in this directory, and docs/decisions/changes.md.

v100-vllm085.name: DGX-1: 8 x Tesla V100-SXM2 32GB, vLLM 0.8.5.post1, float16

why: Its own environment, not a share of another project's: this study pins an engine and a transformers version, and an upgrade made for something else would silently become a new serving snapshot here.
Python 3.10: vLLM 0.8.5.post1 requires >=3.9,<3.13, and 3.10.18 is what this machine already runs.

vllm==0.8.5.post1 is the newest that installs on RHEL 7.9 (glibc 2.17) and the newest that supports Volta. It pins torch==2.6.0 and xformers==0.0.29.post2 itself; torch is named here as well so a change to that pin fails loudly instead of quietly.

transformers==4.57.1 is stated because vLLM 0.8.5 asks only for >=4.51.1, and a fresh install would take whatever is newest -- a 5.x that version was never built against. 4.57.1 is the one already proven on this machine. 4.51.3 is its contemporary, if 4.57.1 ever misbehaves.
pytest so the suite can be run on the server before a run.

float16, not bfloat16: vLLM 0.8.5 refuses bfloat16 below compute capability 8.0 -- 'Bfloat16 is only supported on GPUs with compute capability of at least 8.0' (vllm/worker/worker.py). The checkpoints are bfloat16 and are cast on load.

engine_core v0: vLLM's V1 engine needs compute capability 8.0 ('Need at least Ampere for now', vllm/engine/arg_utils.py), so V1 falls back to V0 here. VLLM_USE_V1=0 states the choice rather than leaving it to the fallback.
attention_backend XFORMERS: FlashAttention-2 does not build for Volta, and vLLM says so and picks XFormers (vllm/platforms/cuda.py).

reasoning_separation client: vLLM 0.8.5 has no qwen3 reasoning parser, and its deepseek_r1 parser files the whole answer as reasoning whenever the reply has no </think> in it -- which is every reply with thinking off, because the template closes the block in the prompt. Qwen's own documentation says it: 'As of vLLM 0.8.5, enable_thinking=False is not compatible with this feature.' So no reasoning parser is started here, and ipb.runner.response does the split.

exclusive_gpus false: the machine is shared, so scripts/serve.sh picks free GPUs and refuses to start beside another job. vLLM measures free memory at startup and fails, or takes memory a neighbour needs.

sm80-vllm0280.name: 80GB GPUs of compute capability 8.0 or newer, vLLM 0.28.0, bfloat16

why: Its own environment, for the same reason as the other one.
Python 3.12: vLLM 0.28.0 requires >=3.10,<3.15.

vllm==0.28.0 pins torch==2.13.0 and asks for transformers>=5.5.3, so neither is named here -- nothing has been verified on that machine yet. Fill `libraries` from pip freeze once it exists, and this file will check the two agree.
openai-harmony==0.0.8 builds every gpt-oss prompt, so its version is part of the snapshot.

vLLM 0.28.0: 0.29.0 was two days old when this was pinned and had made a new model runner the default for every model. A study that runs for months is better on a version that has been out for a while.
bfloat16: what every checkpoint here ships, and what compute capability 8.0 and newer support.

reasoning_separation server: vLLM 0.28.0's qwen3 reasoning parser reads the request's enable_thinking, so the server can be trusted to split thinking from the answer. gpt-oss has no choice: vLLM parses harmony channels itself.
attention_backend null: vLLM picks it from the GPU, and the run records what the server reported.
gpu and gpu_count null: the exact card is not fixed yet. stack_for() takes them from the server at run time and records them; tensor-parallel-size in each serve file assumes 80GB cards.
libraries empty: this environment is not built yet. Fill in the versions the server reports, the way the V100 environment records them.
